'Back in the olden days the only information that was sent to the client machine was the information that they needed. NNTP put all of the 'rendering' on the client side. There is so much data that Voat sends out that is the exact same. Every time a client requests or refreshes Voat's page there is a ton of data that gets resent.

The servers are hit hard rendering it. The bandwidth is wasted sending it. It puts unnecessary strain on Voat's resources.

I copy and pasted the source HTML from my introduction thread and the difference between what Voat sends (and needs to generate) and just the content is much different.

209k Jul 16 09:21 Voat.txt
 4.5k Jul 16 09:23 Voat2.txt

Even gz compressed (== CPU hit) the full HTML version is 5 times larger than the content only plain text.

 25k Jul 16 09:21 Voat.txt.gz
2.2k Jul 16 09:23 Voat2.txt.gz

Look at how RES shifts a lot of stuff from Reddit's servers to the client side. RES adds a ton of features without adding additional load to Reddit's servers or having additional bandwidth requirements. There's absolutely no reason to resend the sidebar HTML everytime I refresh. I've probably wasted gigabytes of your bandwidth in static text so far.

If for no reason other than making the Botnet slightly ineffective. It's much easier to serve 4.5k to a bunch of clients than 209k.

There's no reason that your entire site couldn't be rendered locally by a browser extension and just pinging the servers for very small amounts of data. I do remember reading the Eragon series and last time I put the book down Eragon was doing something called "Scrying." Which is using a puddle to "spy" on other people, kinda like a magic tv screen. But witches actually used this, it's a method of using demons to find hidden knowledge. Obviously gravely sinful, so it can't be great that the main character in the novel is doing this, and he actually called it "scrying" too.

I would say it might be a greater challenge to take out all the magical elements and bring your stories back down to reality. And it will probably end up being a more powerful story.
